Vision Transformer: Patch Prediction, Classification, and Segmentation

This annex documents the frankenstein_vit model class, a Vision Transformer (ViT) implementation that reuses the modality-agnostic HybridLayer stack from the encoder. It supports three tasks: autosupervised masked patch prediction, image classification, and image segmentation (per-pixel or EoMT-style ).

Patch Embedding and Positional Encoding

Following Eq. 1 of the ViT paper, an input image \(x \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W \times C}\) is split into \(N = HW/P^2\) non-overlapping \(P \times P\) patches, each linearly projected to \(D\) dimensions. A Conv2d with kernel and stride \(P\) performs both the splitting and the projection in a single operation. A learnable [CLS] token is optionally prepended, and a learnable positional embedding is added: \[z_0 = \big[\,x_\text{class};\, x_p^1 E;\, x_p^2 E;\, \dots;\, x_p^N E\,\big] + E_\text{pos}, \qquad E \in \mathbb{R}^{(P^2 C) \times D},\quad E_\text{pos} \in \mathbb{R}^{(N+1) \times D}.\]

Positional encoding.

The default positional encoding is a learnable 1D nn.Parameter of shape \((1, N+1, D)\), faithful to the original ViT. The alternative none drops the explicit embedding and relies on RoPE/HoPE applied inside the attention mixers (§20), which is consistent with the encoder’s modality-agnostic handling of rotary embeddings.

[CLS] token.

A learnable [CLS] token is optionally prepended at position \(0\) for classification: the output of position \(0\) after the final normalization is fed to the task head. When [CLS] is disabled, classification relies on Global Average Pooling (GAP) over the patch tokens.

Masked Patch Prediction (Autosupervised)

The autosupervised task mirrors the BERT-style objective of the ViT paper (App. B.1.2). A corruption ratio of \(50\%\) is applied to the patch tokens: of the corrupted subset, \(80\%\) are replaced by a learnable mask token, \(10\%\) are replaced by a random patch, and \(10\%\) are kept unchanged.

Three reconstruction targets are supported:

  1. 3-bit mean color (default): each patch’s mean color is quantized to 3 bits per channel (\(2^{3\times3} = 512\) bins), and a 512-way cross-entropy is computed. This target is the most stable and best-performing in the ViT paper.

  2. \(4\times4\) downsampled 3-bit: the patch is downsampled to a \(4\times4\) grid of 3-bit colors, producing \(16 \times 512\) cross-entropy targets.

  3. Full-patch L2: mean squared error on the raw pixels of the masked patches, equivalent to the pixel reconstruction loss of Masked Autoencoders .

The model predicts only at masked positions; the loss is computed on corrupted patches only, so the network is never asked to reconstruct patches it was allowed to observe.

Image Classification

Classification fine-tuning follows ViT Sec. 3.2:

Pooling.

The representation is pooled either by taking the [CLS] token output at position \(0\) or by Global Average Pooling over the patch tokens.

Head.

A zero-initialized Linear(D, K) projects the pooled vector to \(K\) class logits. The zero initialization guarantees that the fine-tuning starts from the pretrained linear projection and that no class bias is introduced before the first optimizer step.

Loss.

Standard cross-entropy over the \(K\) classes.

Image Segmentation

Two head types are selected by the seg_head_type config field.

Per-Pixel Head (pixel)

A Linear(D, num_seg_classes) is applied per patch token, and the resulting per-patch logits are reshaped to \((H/P, W/P)\). A ViTDet-style transposed-convolution upsampler then scales the logits to the full image resolution \((H, W)\). The training loss is the unweighted sum of cross-entropy and Dice: \[\mathcal{L}_\text{pixel} = \mathrm{CE}(\hat{y}, y) + \mathrm{Dice}(\hat{y}, y).\] This head supports both 1D grayscale (2 classes) and multicolor non-overlapping (\(N+1\) classes) segmentation.

Encoder-only Mask Transformer (eomt)

The EoMT head repurposes the ViT backbone as a mask decoder by splitting the layer stack into two contiguous groups:

  • \(L_1\) (patch-only): the first \(L_1\) blocks process the patch tokens as in a plain ViT.

  • \(L_2\) (patches + queries): the remaining \(L_2\) blocks receive a concatenation of \(K\) learnable object queries and the patch tokens. The multi-head self-attention inside each \(L_2\) block therefore computes all four attention quadrants (patch\(\leftrightarrow\)patch, query\(\leftrightarrow\)query, query\(\to\)patch, patch\(\to\)query) in a single operation, halving the decoder compute relative to an encoder–decoder Mask2Former.

Mask module.

The mask module predicts, for each query, class logits via a linear layer and a mask embedding via a 3-layer MLP. The mask embedding is dot-producted with the upscaled patch feature map \(\tilde{F}_4\) to produce per-pixel mask logits.

Loss with Hungarian matching.

Following Mask2Former, predictions are first matched to ground-truth masks via the Hungarian algorithm, then supervised with: \[\mathcal{L}_\text{eomt} = 5\,\mathrm{BCE} + 5\,\mathrm{Dice} + 2\,\mathrm{CE},\] where the BCE and Dice terms act on mask logits and the CE term acts on class logits (factor 2 for matched queries, factor 0 for the no-object class).

Mask annealing.

A fraction \(P_\text{mask}\) of patches is masked during training, with the fraction decaying polynomially (decay factor \(0.9\)) to \(0\) at inference time. When \(P_\text{mask}=0\) the model reverts to a plain ViT and the \(L_2\) blocks operate on patches only, yielding \(\sim 4\times\) faster inference than at training time while preserving mask quality.

Reuse of Existing Infrastructure

Because the HybridLayer stack is modality-agnostic and operates purely on \((B, S, D)\) tensors, the Vision Transformer reuses the entire encoder-side machinery without modification:

  • Attention mixers: all 34 sequence mixers are available, except engram, which requires discrete token IDs and is therefore not meaningful for continuous patch embeddings.

  • Normalization: all 6 norm variants (LayerNorm, RMSNorm, pRMSNorm, DyT, Derf, FlashNorm).

  • Residuals: all 4 residual variants.

  • Activations: all 42 activation functions (including GLU gated FFN units).

  • Optimizers: all 23 optimizer families with prefixed per-parameter-group hyperparameter control.

  • Training configuration: the three vision tasks read batch_size, num_epochs, optimizer, scheduler_type, grad_clip_max_norm, and checkpointing from the same top-level training: block as mlm and causal_lm. The optional training.<task>: sub-block carries only task-specific knobs: label_smoothing for classification, and seg_loss_bce_weight / seg_loss_dice_weight / seg_loss_ce_weight / mask_annealing_factor for EoMT segmentation.

The FrankensteinViT class mirrors the FrankensteinDecoder wrapper pattern: it owns a PatchEmbed module, a HybridLayer stack, and a task-specific head, and it forces mode=’encoder’ so that the bidirectional attention pattern required by vision tasks is preserved.

PyTorch Pseudocode

The forward pass for each task is sketched below.

Classification.

\(x \gets \texttt{patch\_\allowbreak embed}(\texttt{pixel\_\allowbreak values})\) \(x \gets [\,\texttt{cls\_\allowbreak token}\,;\, x\,]\) \(x \gets x + \texttt{pos\_\allowbreak embed}\) \(x \gets \texttt{dropout}(x)\) \(x \gets \texttt{layer}(x)\) \(x \gets \texttt{final\_\allowbreak norm}(x)\) \(\texttt{logits} \gets \texttt{head}(x[:, 0])\)

Masked patch prediction.

\(x \gets \texttt{patch\_\allowbreak embed}(\texttt{pixel\_\allowbreak values})\) \((x,\, m) \gets \texttt{mask}(x,\, r=0.5)\) \(x \gets [\,\texttt{cls\_\allowbreak token}\,;\, x\,] + \texttt{pos\_\allowbreak embed}\) \(x \gets \texttt{dropout}(x)\) \(x \gets \texttt{layer}(x)\) \(x \gets \texttt{final\_\allowbreak norm}(x)\) \(\hat{y} \gets \texttt{head}(x[:, 1:])\) \(\mathcal{L} \gets \texttt{loss}(\hat{y}[m],\, y[m])\)

EoMT segmentation.

\(x \gets \texttt{patch\_\allowbreak embed}(\texttt{pixel\_\allowbreak values})\) \(x \gets x + \texttt{pos\_\allowbreak embed}\) \(x \gets \texttt{mask\_\allowbreak anneal}(x)\) \(x \gets \texttt{layer}(x)\) \(q \gets \texttt{learnable\_\allowbreak queries}\) \(x \gets [\,x;\, q\,]\) \(x \gets \texttt{layer}(x)\) \(\hat{c},\, \hat{m} \gets \texttt{mask\_\allowbreak module}(x_\text{patches},\, x_\text{queries},\, \tilde{F}_4)\) \((\sigma,\, \hat{y}_\sigma) \gets \texttt{Hungarian}(\hat{c},\, \hat{m},\, y)\) \(\mathcal{L} \gets 5\,\mathrm{BCE} + 5\,\mathrm{Dice} + 2\,\mathrm{CE}\)

Model-Wide Positional Encodings

This annex documents the unified positional-encoding (PE) subsystem that applies a single model.positional_encoding choice to every attention mixer in the network. The schema contract is: \[\begin{gathered} \texttt{positional\_\allowbreak encoding} \in \{\texttt{rope},\ \texttt{hope},\ \texttt{nope},\ \texttt{alibi},\ \texttt{bam},\ \texttt{pape},\\ \texttt{pape\_\allowbreak efficient},\ \texttt{pape\_\allowbreak ri},\ \texttt{sinusoidal\_\allowbreak absolute},\ \texttt{sinusoidal\_\allowbreak rotary},\\ \texttt{learned\_\allowbreak absolute},\ \texttt{none}\} \end{gathered}\] The implementation lives in and the shared injection helpers in . Bibliography keys cited here resolve against .

Architecture: One Shared Module, Per-Mixer Opt-Out

A single PE module is built once in the encoder (FrankensteinEncoder or FrankensteinViT) via build_pos_encoder(config) and injected into every HybridLayer, which forwards it to each mixer’s __init__(config, pos_encoder=None) and forward(..., pos_encoder=None).

Each mixer carries a per-mixer use_pe flag (<mixer>_use_pe, default True for attention mixers, False for recurrent/decay mixers such as retnet, mamba, ode, gla, deltanet, mtla, and the six Falcon mixers falcon{1,2,3,1a,2a,3a}). When use_pe is False the mixer ignores the injected module entirely.

The PE is applied in two phases via the shared helpers apply_pe_to_qk() (called before the attention-score computation) and apply_pe_to_scores() (called after). The helper dispatches on the PE type and falls through to a no-op when the mixer’s use_pe flag is False.

Injection Styles

The 11 enum values fall into four injection styles:

  1. Rotation (rope, hope, sinusoidal_rotary): rotates the query and key tensors before the score computation. The inner product \(\mathbf{q}_i^\top\mathbf{k}_j\) becomes a function of the relative offset \(i-j\).

  2. Score bias (alibi): adds a distance-proportional bias to the attention-score matrix after it is computed.

  3. Q/K augmentation (pape, pape_efficient, pape_ri): concatenates extra positional dimensions onto the query and key vectors before the dot product, increasing the effective head dimension.

  4. Additive at embedding level (sinusoidal_absolute, learned_absolute): added directly to the token embeddings before the first layer; no per-mixer action is taken in the attention block.

nope and none are both no-ops: nope explicitly disables positional encoding (the model must learn position implicitly), while none is the null module returned by the factory when no PE is desired.

Mathematical Formulations

RoPE — Rotary Position Embedding

RoPE rotates each head’s query and key by an angle proportional to the token index. For head dimension \(d_h\) and token position \(m\), the rotation matrix \(\mathbf{R}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{d_h \times d_h}\) acts on 2-D sub-spaces \((x_{2i}, x_{2i+1})\): \[\mathbf{R}_m = \operatorname{diag}\!\left( \begin{bmatrix}\cos m\theta_0 & -\sin m\theta_0 \\ \sin m\theta_0 & \cos m\theta_0\end{bmatrix}, \dots, \begin{bmatrix}\cos m\theta_{d_h/2-1} & -\sin m\theta_{d_h/2-1} \\ \sin m\theta_{d_h/2-1} & \cos m\theta_{d_h/2-1}\end{bmatrix} \right),\] with frequencies \(\theta_i = \texttt{rope\_\allowbreak base}^{-2i/d_h}\). The attention score becomes \(\mathbf{q}_m^\top \mathbf{R}_{m-n} \mathbf{k}_n\), a function of the relative offset \(m{-}n\). A rope_scaling factor \(s\) rescales the effective position to \(m/s\) for length-extrapolation modes.

HoPE — Hyperbolic Rotary Positional Encoding

HoPE generalises RoPE to the hyperbolic geometry of the Lorentz model. Instead of Euclidean rotations, HoPE applies Lorentz rotations built from hyperbolic functions, enforcing a monotonic decay of attention weights with increasing token distance — a property RoPE lacks because its oscillatory attention pattern can re-spike at long ranges. RoPE is recovered as a special case. The hope_base and hope_damping knobs control the hyperbolic frequency and the decay rate.

NoPE — No Positional Encoding

NoPE is the explicit absence of any positional injection. The model must discover position implicitly from the causal mask (decoder) or from the data itself. The cited work shows that NoPE outperforms explicit PE methods (including RoPE and ALiBi) on length-generalisation benchmarks while requiring no additional computation, because a causal-attention decoder can implicitly encode relative position through its attention patterns.

ALiBi — Attention with Linear Biases

ALiBi does not modify the embeddings or the query/key vectors. Instead it adds a static, head-specific linear bias to the attention-score matrix: \[\text{score}_{i,j}^{(h)} = \frac{\mathbf{q}_i^{(h)\top}\mathbf{k}_j^{(h)}}{\sqrt{d_h}} - m_h \cdot (i - j), \qquad m_h = \frac{1}{2^{\lfloor h / \lceil H/8 \rceil \rfloor}},\] where \(m_h\) is a geometric slope per head \(h\) and the bias penalises distant keys. The alibi_num_heads knob controls the slope schedule’s head count. ALiBi enables length extrapolation: a model trained on 1024 tokens generalises to 2048 without retraining.

BAM — Bayesian Attention Mechanism

BAM reframes positional encoding as a probabilistic prior over positions and unifies existing methods: NoPE corresponds to a Uniform prior, ALiBi to a Uniform\(\times\)Laplace prior. The practical instantiation, GGD-BAM, adds a Generalized-Gaussian relative-position bias matrix \(\mathbf{B}\) to the attention logits, exactly like ALiBi but with a non-linear, learnable shape: \[B_{i,j}^{(h)} = -\bigl(|j - \alpha_h \, i - \mu_h| + \varepsilon\bigr)^{\beta_h}, \qquad \alpha_h = e^{-\theta_\beta^{(h)}\,\theta_\alpha^{(h)}} \ge 0,\] with per-head learnable \(\theta_\alpha, \theta_\beta\) (init bam_theta_init=0, the Uniform prior) and optional location \(\theta_\mu\) (fixed to 0 by default via bam_learn_mu=false). The floor \(\varepsilon\) (bam_eps, default \(10^{-5}\)) stabilises the exponentiation when \(\beta < 0\), a relaxed regime that suppresses local context and acts as a long-range “retrieval head”. Special cases: \(\beta=1, \mu=0\) recovers ALiBi; \(\beta=2\) gives a Normal prior; \(0<\beta<1\) yields heavier tails than Laplace. The paper pairs BAM with Scalable Softmax (SSMax), a transversal logit rescale \(s\cdot\ln(n)\) (learnable per-head \(s\)) that counteracts “attention fading” and is composable with any PE via the top-level use_ssmax flag. BAM SSMax achieves accurate information retrieval at \(500\times\) the training context length.

PaPE — Parabolic Position Encoding

PaPE is a vision-centric encoding that augments the query and key with extra positional dimensions built from parabolic basis functions. Given \(P\) parabolas (pape_num_parabolas) and \(S\) positions (pape_num_positions), the positional feature for coordinate \(\mathbf{p} \in \mathbb{R}^D\) is \[\phi_k(\mathbf{p}) = \sum_{j=1}^{S} \alpha_{k,j}\, f_j(\mathbf{p}), \qquad f_j(\mathbf{p}) = -\|\mathbf{p} - \mathbf{c}_j\|^2 + b_j,\] a sum of \(S\) paraboloids centred at \(\mathbf{c}_j\) with offset \(b_j\). The \(P \cdot S\) extra dimensions are concatenated to the query and key before the dot product, so the effective head dimension grows from \(d_h\) to \(d_h + P \cdot S\). Three variants are provided:

  • pape — the reference implementation.

  • pape_efficient — a pure-PyTorch reformulation that avoids custom Triton kernels while preserving the same math.

  • pape_ri — the rotation-invariant variant (PaPE-RI in the paper), which satisfies rotation invariance by construction and is controlled by pape_rotation_invariant.

PaPE is designed for \(n\)-D vision tokens (images, video, event cameras, point clouds) and is the recommended PE for the ViT path.

Sinusoidal Absolute

The original Transformer absolute encoding adds a fixed sinusoidal vector to the token embedding: \[\text{PE}_{(m,2i)} = \sin\!\left(\frac{m}{\texttt{sinusoidal\_\allowbreak base}^{2i/d}}\right), \quad \text{PE}_{(m,2i+1)} = \cos\!\left(\frac{m}{\texttt{sinusoidal\_\allowbreak base}^{2i/d}}\right),\] with sinusoidal_max_len capping the precomputed table and sinusoidal_scale multiplying the embedding. This is an additive PE: it is applied once at the embedding level and the mixers do not apply any per-layer PE.

Sinusoidal Rotary

A rotary variant of the sinusoidal encoding: the same sinusoidal frequencies are used to build a rotation matrix applied to the query and key (as in RoPE), but with the sinusoidal_base and sinusoidal_scale knobs. This is a rotation-style PE applied per-layer via apply_pe_to_qk.

Learned Absolute

A learnable absolute encoding: an \(\texttt{learned\_\allowbreak max\_\allowbreak len} \times d\) parameter matrix is added to the token embeddings at the embedding level. Initialisation standard deviation is controlled by learned_init_std. As with sinusoidal absolute, the mixers take no per-layer action.

Per-Mixer use_pe Flags

Each mixer exposes a <mixer>_use_pe config field (e.g. standard_use_pe, titan_use_pe). The defaults are:

  • True (attention mixers): standard, titan, sigmoid, gated_softmax, gqa, all latent mixers (mla, gqla, mlra, tucker, iha, gta, cca, ccgqa, gma), all sparse mixers (longformer, bigbird, sparse_transformer, sparsek, nsa, msa, sparda, fasa, sparge), and engram, and memory (RoPE on the scoring pair only; values are built from the unrotated keys).

  • False (recurrent/decay mixers): retnet, retnet, mamba, ode, gla, deltanet, gated_deltanet, gated_deltanet2, hgrn2, fox, kda, mtla.

The False default for recurrent/decay mixers reflects that these architectures bake their own temporal/positional inductive bias into their recurrence (e.g. RetNet’s complex rotation, Mamba’s selective scan). Overriding use_pe=True is allowed but is typically redundant.

Vision Transformer Unification

The ViT path (FrankensteinViT) previously used its own pos_embedding_type field with values learned_1d, none. This has been unified with the model-wide enum: learned_1d is migrated to learned_absolute, and none maps to none. The ViT builds the same build_pos_encoder(config) module and injects it into its HybridLayers, so a ViT can now use RoPE, HoPE, ALiBi, PaPE, or any other PE in the enum.

Legacy Compatibility

The legacy use_hope boolean flag is deprecated and mapped to the new enum: use_hope=True \(\to\) positional_encoding=hope, use_hope=False \(\to\) positional_encoding=rope. The per-mixer positional_encoding override that previously existed only on titan is now a no-op: the model-wide enum is the single source of truth, and the TitanAttention allow-list that restricted PE to {hope, rope, none, nope} has been removed — all 12 values now work with every mixer.

SSOG: Separable Sum of Gaussians Attention

This annex covers SSOG (Separable Sum of Gaussians), a geometric-field attention mixer. SSOG replaces the content-scored interaction of scaled dot-product attention with a learned mixture of Gaussians over relative position: each head owns a handful of Gaussian atoms—five numbers per atom, a center offset \((\mu_y, \mu_x)\), a width per axis \((\sigma_y, \sigma_x)\) and a mixture weight \(\lambda\)—forming a fixed field over the displacement between tokens. There are no query–key dot products anywhere: content never scores content, it only steers the field through small bounded residuals.

Because a 2D Gaussian factorises into a product of two 1D Gaussians, applying the field is two 1D filter passes per atom (rows, then columns of a \(\sqrt{N} \times \sqrt{N}\) token raster) followed by a \(\lambda\)-mix contraction. The induced \(N \times N\) attention matrix never exists, so the attention-specific cost is \(\mathcal{O}(R \cdot N \sqrt{N} \cdot d)\) for \(R\) atoms instead of \(\mathcal{O}(N^2 \cdot d)\). SSOG also skips the query and key projections entirely, paying \(2d^2\) of projections per layer instead of the \(4d^2\) of SDPA. In the reference recipe the full mechanism beats its matched SDPA twin on ImageNet-1k (65.28% vs 64.34% at \(\sim\)3M params; 72.02% vs 71.84% at \(\sim\)12M) while being \(\sim\)20% smaller and \(\sim\)30% cheaper per forward, and by +17 points on CIFAR-100 at matched recipe.

Mathematical Formulation

Let tokens be the row-major raster of a \(G_h \times G_w\) grid. The attention weight from token \(p\) to token \(q\) is the softmax-tempered log-sum-exp of the atom log-weights evaluated at their displacement: \[A(p, q) = \operatorname{softmax}_q\!\left( \tfrac{1}{\tau}\, s(p, q) \right), \qquad s(p, q) = \operatorname{logsumexp}_r \big( \log \lambda_r + \log \mathcal{N}(p - q;\ \mu_r, \sigma_r) \big),\] where \(\tau\) is a learnable temperature and \(\mathcal{N}(\cdot\,;\mu_r, \sigma_r)\) is a 2D Gaussian with diagonal covariance. Since the 2D Gaussian factorises, the softmaxed field applies separably: per axis, \(a_y[i, j] = \operatorname{softmax}_j(\log \mathcal{N}(\Delta y_{ij}; \mu_y, \sigma_y) / \tau)\) and analogously \(a_x\), followed by \[Y = \sum_{r=1}^{R} \lambda_r\, \big( a_x^{(r)} \big( a_y^{(r)}\, V \big) \big), \qquad V = x W_V,\] i.e. three einsum contractions per layer. With content steering (lookat) enabled, zero-initialised linear probes predict bounded per-token residuals on the field parameters behind cold-started softplus gates: \[\mu \leftarrow \mu_0 + s_\mu \cdot m \cdot \tanh(W_\mu x), \qquad \sigma \leftarrow \sigma_0 \, e^{s_\sigma \tanh(W_\sigma x)}, \qquad \lambda \leftarrow \operatorname{softmax}\big( \log \lambda_0 + s_\lambda \tanh(W_\lambda x) \big),\] with \(m\) the maximum offset in grid cells and gate scales \(s_\bullet = \operatorname{softplus}(\cdot)\) initialised at \(-8\) (\(\approx 3 \times 10^{-4}\)), so the model begins as a frozen geometric field and learns how far to open each content tap. Widths are reparameterised as \(\sigma = \operatorname{softplus}(\omega) + \epsilon + \sigma_{\text{floor}}\) to stay strictly positive.

Algorithmic Pseudocode

Input: hidden state \(x \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times N \times d}\) as a \(G_h \times G_w\) raster, atoms \(\{\mu_r, \omega_r, \log \lambda_r\}_{r=1}^{R}\) per head, temperature \(\tau\) \(V \gets x W_V\) reshaped to \((B, G_h, G_w, H, d_h)\) \(\sigma_r \gets \operatorname{softplus}(\omega_r) + \epsilon + \sigma_{\text{floor}}\) \(\mu, \sigma, \lambda \gets\) bounded per-token residuals via zero-init probes and gates \(a_y \gets \operatorname{softmax}\!\big(\log \mathcal{N}(\Delta y; \mu_y, \sigma_y) / \tau\big)\), \(a_x \gets\) analogously \(Y \gets \sum_r \lambda_r\, a_x^{(r)} \big( a_y^{(r)} V \big)\) Output: \(\mathbf{Y} W_O\) reshaped to \((B, N, d)\)

Key Characteristics

  • Training complexity: \(\mathcal{O}(R \cdot N \sqrt{N} \cdot d)\) for fixed \(R\) atoms—near-linear by geometry alone, not by kernel approximation.

  • Inference complexity: same per-forward cost; encoder-only (the separable field has no causal formulation), so there are no KV-cache semantics.

  • Trainable: atoms \(\{\mu, \omega, \log\lambda\}\), temperature, and the steering probes are fully differentiable; cold-started gates open during optimisation.

  • Strengths: strong geometric prior (+17 pts over SDPA on small data at matched recipe; beats SDPA on ImageNet-1k at 3M and 12M params with \(\sim\)20% fewer parameters and \(\sim\)30% fewer FLOPs); inherently interpretable (each head is a few plottable blobs—early layers become convolutions in disguise, middle layers strip detectors, late layers go global); the field lives on coordinates, granting zero-shot resolution transfer.

  • Limitations: encoder-only; requires a fixed \(G_h \times G_w\) row-major raster (ViT needs cls_token=false; sequences need an explicit \(1 \times L\) grid); the per-query steering kernels add a memory term; language results are unproven—content scoring is likely load-bearing there.

Fast-Weight Attention for Continual Learning

This annex covers the Falcon family , a fast-weight attention framework that treats the recurrent fast-weight state transition as an online continual-learning rule under read-after-write (RAW) autoregressive semantics. The framework’s central observation is one of temporal alignment: for the prefix-prediction objective, the local fast-memory example revealed at step \(t\) is the prefix-aligned pair \((x_t, y_t) = (\phi(k_{t-1}),\, v_t)\) — one step shifted relative to the same-step association \((\phi(k_t), v_t)\) used by DeltaNet and standard linear attention. The same-step pairing remains causal, but it optimizes a different internal objective. The framework derives normalized first-order updates for two objectives (squared-error regression and negative inner product) and three step-size structures (scalar, per-column, sliding window), giving six variants: Falcon-1/2/3 (regression family) and Falcon-1A/2A/3A (inner-product family). All six are implemented in the codebase under model.attention.falcon with a shared configuration block, each providing both a recurrent reference scan and an SSD-style chunk-parallel kernel.

Preliminaries: Alignment, Normalization, and Stability

Read-after-write semantics.

With feature maps \(\phi(k_t)\) (QK-RMSNorm by default, \(\ell_2\) norm optional), the prefix-aligned stream sets \(x_t = \phi(k_{t-1})\) for \(t \ge 2\) with boundary sentinel \(x_1 = 0\); the readout is \(o_t = S_t^\top \phi(q_t)\). The write at step \(t\) therefore updates the memory before the query at step \(t+1\) reads it, so no token’s key ever associates with its own value.

Normalized first-order step sizes.

A gradient step on the local objective \(\ell_t(S)\) with the objective-matched denominator gives \[\eta_t = \frac{\beta_t}{\text{statistic}_t + \lambda_t + \varepsilon}, \qquad \beta_t \in (0, 2),\] where the statistic is the squared key energy \(\|x_t\|^2\) (Falcon-1/1A/2/2A), the window spectral statistic \(\mu_t^{(B)} = \lambda_{\max}(X^\top X)/B_t\) (Falcon-3), or the window mean energy \(\bar{E}_t^{(B)}\) (Falcon-3A). Objective-matched normalization guarantees per-step descent and removes the scale sensitivity of fixed learning rates. The plasticity gain \(\beta_t\), the forgetting ridge \(\lambda_t\), the temporal alignment, and the rehearsal window \(B\) are thereby four previously entangled knobs, separated.

Positive-decay renormalization.

When \(\lambda_t > 0\), the per-step shrinkage \(\alpha_t = \min(\eta_t \lambda_t,\, 1 - \varepsilon_\gamma)\) must be applied stably. The implementation clamps \(\alpha_t\) strictly below \(1\), computes chunk-local log-prefixes in fp32 via \(\log(1 - \alpha_t)\) and cumulative sums, rescales the drivers to the no-decay domain (\(\tilde{\eta}_t = \eta_t / \gamma_t\), \(\tilde{v}_t = v_t / c_{t-1}\) with \(c_{t-1} = \prod_{r \le t-1} \gamma_r\)), and rescales outputs and the emitted state back by the accumulated \(\delta\). Boundary sentinels are \((\alpha_1, \gamma_1) = (0, 1)\) and \(\eta_1 = 0\), so the first step is a pure read.

The Regression Family (Falcon-1/2/3)

The squared-error objective on the shifted pair is \[\ell_t(S) = \tfrac{1}{2}\|v_t - S^\top x_t\|^2 + \tfrac{\lambda_t}{2}\|S\|_F^2, \qquad \nabla_S \ell_t = x_t (S^\top x_t - v_t)^\top + \lambda_t S,\] which is \(L_t\)-smooth with \(L_t = \|x_t\|^2 + \lambda_t\).

Falcon-1: Scalar NLMS Regression

The scalar delta-rule variant — the classical NLMS recursion of adaptive filtering upgraded with the shifted write stream and an explicit ridge: \[S_t = (1 - \eta_t \lambda_t)\, S_{t-1} + \eta_t\, x_t \big(v_t - S_{t-1}^\top x_t\big)^\top, \qquad o_t = S_t^\top \phi(q_t).\] With \(\varepsilon = 0\), \(\lambda_t = 0\) and the unshifted assignment \(x_t = \phi(k_t)\) this recovers DeltaNet exactly. The eigenstructure of the transition \(A_t = \gamma_t I - \eta_t x_t x_t^\top\) (with \(\gamma_t = 1 - \eta_t\lambda_t\)) shows that the write direction contracts by \(1 - \beta_t\) while the orthogonal subspace carries \(\gamma_t\): \(\beta_t > 1\) yields a stable sign-flip along the write direction, useful for state tracking. The chunk-parallel form uses the WY representation \(\prod_s (I - \eta_s x_s x_s^\top) = I - U T U^\top\) with a single-residual unit-lower-triangular solve \(L = \operatorname{tril}(G, -1) + I\) where \(G = X^\top X\) (Algorithm 8 of the paper), after the positive-decay renormalization.

Falcon-2: Per-Column NLMS Regression

The ridge loss decomposes across value coordinates, so each value channel \(j\) receives its own step size while sharing the NLMS normalizer: \[\eta_{j,t} = \frac{\beta_{j,t}}{\|x_t\|^2 + \lambda_t + \varepsilon}, \qquad S_t = S_{t-1}\big(I - \lambda_t \operatorname{Diag}(\boldsymbol{\eta}_t)\big) + x_t \big(\boldsymbol{\eta}_t \odot \mathbf{r}_t\big)^\top .\] The chunk-parallel kernel forms the shared key Gram \(G = X^\top X\) and solves the batch of per-channel unit-lower-triangular systems \(L_j = I + \operatorname{tril}\big(G \odot (\Sigma_j \Sigma_j^\top), -1\big)\) with \(\Sigma = \sqrt{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}}}\) (Algorithm 1). Defined but not separately benchmarked in the paper.

Falcon-3: Sliding-Window Minibatch Regression

Bounded rehearsal: each step regresses the fast memory on the last \(B_t \le B\) prefix-aligned pairs, with all window residuals evaluated at the pre-update state \(S_{t-1}\): \[\mu_t = \frac{\lambda_{\max}\big(X_{\mathcal{I}_t}^\top X_{\mathcal{I}_t}\big)}{B_t}, \qquad \eta_t = \frac{\beta_t}{\mu_t + \lambda_t + \varepsilon}, \qquad S_t = (1 - \eta_t \lambda_t)\, S_{t-1} + \frac{\eta_t}{B_t} \sum_{j \in \mathcal{I}_t} x_j \big(v_j - S_{t-1}^\top x_j\big)^\top ,\] with \(\mathcal{I}_t = \{\max(2, t - B + 1), \dots, t\}\). Window-averaging keeps the update magnitude invariant to \(B\): each pair is replayed in exactly \(B\) consecutive updates at weight \(1/B\), so its cumulative injection is \(\eta\)-independent of \(B\). The state alone is not Markov: exact continuation requires a FIFO tail of the last \(B - 1\) pairs, and the chunk kernels gather an extended slice with \(|\mathcal{J}| \le C + B - 1\). The chunk-parallel form is a rank-\(B\) affine recurrence solved by block forward substitution over the (time \(\times\) rank) extended index space, with same-time rank components uncoupled (Algorithm 3).

The Inner-Product Family (Falcon-1A/2A/3A)

The negative inner-product objective \[\ell_t^{\mathrm{ip}}(S) = -\langle S^\top x_t,\, v_t \rangle + \tfrac{\lambda_t}{2}\|S\|_F^2 \qquad \Rightarrow \qquad \nabla_S \ell_t^{\mathrm{ip}} = -x_t v_t^\top + \lambda_t S\] yields purely additive (Hebbian) writes with energy-normalized gains.

Falcon-1A and Falcon-2A

\[\begin{gathered} \text{Falcon-1A:}\quad S_t = \gamma_t S_{t-1} + \eta_t\, x_t v_t^\top, \quad \gamma_t = 1 - \min(\eta_t \lambda_t,\, 1 - \varepsilon_\gamma);\\ \text{Falcon-2A:}\quad S_t = S_{t-1}\operatorname{Diag}(\boldsymbol{\gamma}_t) + x_t (\boldsymbol{\eta}_t \odot v_t)^\top . \end{gathered}\] With \(\lambda_t = 0\) and the unshifted assignment this is exactly standard linear attention / Mamba-2 accumulation; the shifted stream makes it the one-step-shifted next-latent variant. The A-family’s denominator is not required by curvature (the objective is linear) — it retains the energy-normalized write as a magnitude stabilizer. The chunk-parallel form is decay-mask linear attention with \(M_{t,i} = \eta_i \prod_{r=i+1}^{t} \gamma_r\) (per-channel masks for Falcon-2A).

Falcon-3A: Sliding-Window Inner-Product

The windowed additive variant — the family’s best length-extrapolation configuration: \[\bar{N}_t^{(B)} = \frac{1}{B_t} \sum_{j \in \mathcal{I}_t} x_j v_j^\top, \quad \bar{E}_t^{(B)} = \frac{1}{B_t} \sum_{j \in \mathcal{I}_t} \|x_j\|^2, \quad \eta_t = \frac{\beta_t}{\bar{E}_t^{(B)} + \lambda_t + \varepsilon}, \qquad S_t = \gamma_t S_{t-1} + \eta_t\, \bar{N}_t^{(B)} .\] The window-banded decay mask factors as \(M = D \cdot \operatorname{Diag}(\boldsymbol{\eta}) \cdot A\), where \(A\) is the \(B\)-banded window operator and \(D\) the causal decay kernel, evaluated over the extended slice (Algorithm 4).

Configuration Interface

All six variants share one nested block, model.attention.falcon, selected through the layer_pattern entries falcon1, falcon2, falcon3, falcon1a, falcon2a, falcon3a:

Shared Falcon configuration knobs (model.attention.falcon). Each variant additionally exposes a per-mixer positional-encoding opt-out falcon{1,2,3,1a,2a,3a}_use_pe, default False like other recurrent/decay mixers.
Key Default Description
chunk_size \(64\) Chunk size of the chunk-parallel kernels; null selects the recurrent reference scan
qk_norm rms_norm QK normalization (rms_norm or l2_norm); RMSNorm computed in fp32
beta_mode ctx_eta Plasticity gate parameterization: static, ctx_beta (content-conditioned gain), or ctx_eta (content-conditioned normalized step)
lambda_mode ctx Forgetting gate: static or ctx (scale-couples with the detached curvature statistic)
beta / lambda \(1.0\) / \(0.0\) Static gain and ridge (used when the corresponding mode is static)
window \(4\) Sliding window \(B\) (Falcon-3 / Falcon-3A only)
short_conv / conv_kernel true / \(4\) Causal depth-wise short convolutions on the q/k/v projections
eps / eps_gamma \(10^{-6}\) / \(10^{-4}\) Step-size stabilizer and positive-decay clamp floor

Implementation notes: the recurrent and chunk-parallel kernels are verified numerically equivalent (chunk \(\equiv\) recurrent to \(\le 3.6 \times 10^{-7}\) across all six variants, including decay, multi-chunk, and windowed paths); gradients flow through the fp32 triangular-solve islands (feature drivers take only \(\sqrt{\tilde{\eta}}\) while value targets take \(\sqrt{\tilde{\eta}}\, e^{-u_{t-1}}\), with the square root clamped at \(10^{-12}\) for NaN-free backward at the \(\eta = 0\) boundary); positive exponents are clamped at \(80\).

Published Results

Language modeling results reported by at 124M parameters. On variable-digit addition length extrapolation (33–48 digits), Falcon-3A.3 reaches 87.2% mean accuracy versus 65.8% for a RoPE Transformer and 85.9% for Falcon-1A.3: the inner-product family carries arithmetic, while the regression family carries perplexity.

Relation to Prior Work

  • DeltaNet: the delta rule is the squared-error one-gradient-descent step with the same-step pairing; Falcon recovers it with the critical index shift plus objective-matched normalization and explicit \(\lambda_t\) shrinkage.

  • Gated DeltaNet: adds a free learned carry gate; Falcon derives the carry \(\gamma_t = 1 - \eta_t \lambda_t\) from the local objective and the normalized step-size parameterization instead of adding an independent gate, and defaults to QK-RMSNorm rather than \(\ell_2\) normalization.

  • Linear attention / Mamba-2: the additive numerator is one gradient step on the inner-product objective with the unshifted assignment; the chunkwise kernels reuse the SSD scheme.

  • TTT / Titans / ATLAS: fast-weight updates as test-time training; Falcon-3 is a sliding-window specialization of the internal-objective view with strict next-latent alignment.

  • Adaptive filtering (LMS/NLMS/RLS): Falcon imports the stability and normalization principles of NLMS into fast-weight attention under strict causality.

When to Use Each Variant

  1. Falcon-1: best language-modeling perplexity of the family (FineEdu 17.10, beating Gated DeltaNet 17.32); principled forgetting tied to the local objective.

  2. Falcon-2: finer-grained plasticity than Falcon-1 at the cost of heavier per-channel chunk kernels; unbenchmarked in the paper.

  3. Falcon-3: controlled rehearsal horizon with exact window statistics; most complex kernel.

  4. Falcon-1A: simple and stable additive variant; second-best length extrapolation (85.9%).

  5. Falcon-2A: channel-wise forgetting granularity; unbenchmarked.

  6. Falcon-3A: best length extrapolation of the paper (87.2% on 33–48-digit addition); carries arithmetic tasks.

KV Cache and Incremental Decoding

Autoregressive decoding is dominated by a structural asymmetry: the prefill stage processes the whole prompt in one quadratic pass, while each decode step appends a single token and needs only one new query row against an already-computed history. Recomputing the full sequence at every step turns generation into an \(\mathcal{O}(S^2)\)-per-token procedure; maintaining the per-layer history turns it into \(\mathcal{O}(S)\) per token with constant-size work per new position. This annex documents the toolkit’s KV-cache subsystem (src/model/cache/), the correctness contracts that make cached and uncached execution numerically interchangeable, the per-family incremental recipes, and the write-time quantizers and read-time eviction policies layered on top of it.

Three design commitments frame everything below. First, the cache is opt-in: with inference.kv_cache.enabled unset (default), generation executes the original full-recompute loop bit-identically. Second, the cache is central and declarative: a single manager is threaded through the model, and a per-mixer capability registry decides which layers may cache — never the other way around. Third, the cache is never fatal (decision D5): a layer whose source formulation does not admit an exact incremental form silently runs uncached, so enabling the cache can only ever change speed, not correctness or availability.

Motivation and Scope

Let \(S\) be the prompt length and \(T\) the number of generated tokens. Without a cache, step \(t\) feeds \(S+t-1\) tokens through every layer and discards all intermediate keys and values, for total attention work \[\mathcal{O}\!\left(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} (S+t)^2\right) \;=\; \mathcal{O}\!\left(T S^2 + T^2 S + T^3\right).\] With a cache, the prefill costs \(\mathcal{O}(S^2)\) once and each decode step costs \(\mathcal{O}(S+t)\): \[\mathcal{O}\!\left(S^2 + \sum_{t=0}^{T-1}(S+t)\right) \;=\; \mathcal{O}\!\left(S^2 + TS + T^2\right).\] The difference is the familiar one between re-encoding a conversation and continuing it.

The subsystem covers every one of the forty-seven dispatchable layer types. Twenty-nine have parity-tested incremental branches; the remainder are registered with an explicit, paper-based rationale for running uncached (§28.4.5). Quantization and eviction are orthogonal to the mixer mathematics: codecs transform tensors at write time and policies act at read time, so the same int8 or int4_kivi codec serves a dense, latent or ring slot without per-mixer code .

Cache Architecture

Central Manager and Layer Identity

The unit of caching is a logical layer, not a module. The encoder may re-execute the same physical stack num_loops times (looped depth) and, under Hyperloop, partitions it into a begin block, a looped middle block and an end block. The same HybridLayer object therefore plays several distinct roles during one forward pass. The cache keys every slot by the global logical layer index \[\ell \;=\; 0,\dots,\, \texttt{num\_\allowbreak layers}\times\texttt{num\_\allowbreak loops}-1 ,\] which the encoder already threads into every mixer call. Two logical roles never share storage even though they share weights.

prompt ids \(\mathbf{x}_{1:S}\); generation config \(\theta\); model \(f\) generated ids \(\mathcal{C} \gets \textsc{Cache.new}(f,\theta)\) \(\mathbf{L}, \mathcal{C} \gets f(\mathbf{x}_{1:S}; \text{past}=\mathcal{C}, \text{use\_\allowbreak cache}=\top, \text{return\_\allowbreak cache}=\top)\) \(\mathbf{z} \gets \mathbf{L}_{:,S,:}\) \(y \gets \textsc{Sample}(\mathbf{z};\theta)\) append \(y\) to the output \(p \gets \mathcal{C}.\text{next\_\allowbreak position}()\) \(\mathbf{L}, \mathcal{C} \gets f(y; \text{past}=\mathcal{C}, \text{use\_\allowbreak cache}=\top, \text{cache\_\allowbreak position}=p, \text{return\_\allowbreak cache}=\top)\) \(\mathbf{z} \gets \mathbf{L}_{:,-1,:}\)

The manager owns the per-layer slot dictionary, a FIFO of recent token ids (consumed by token-level mixers such as Engram), a write cursor advanced by each forward, and the resolved quantization codec and eviction policy. Slot creation is lazy and driven by the layer on first use, so a heterogeneous layer_pattern — say a dense layer, a latent layer and a recurrent layer in one stack — holds three different slot kinds without special-casing. Rollback is a first-class operation: truncate(n) keeps the first \(n\) positions across all slots (cheap list truncation with length bookkeeping; recurrent-state slots are no-ops because they are not position-indexed), which is the primitive required by speculative decoding and early-exit verification .

Typed Slots

Six slot kinds cover the taxonomy of §28.4. Position-indexed slots store an ordered list of parts; a part is either full precision or an encoded payload, and reading concatenates \(\big[\text{sinks} \mid \text{history} \mid \text{protected window}\big]\).

0.98l L0.34 X Slot kind & Stores & Used by
kv & post-RoPE keys and values \((\text{B},H_{kv},T,d)\); absolute positions; optional per-token extras & quadratic softmax mixers
latent_kv & named low-rank streams: latent \(\mathbf{c}_{KV}\), decoupled RoPE key, grouped keys, latent values & latent family
state & one recurrent matrix (+ gate accumulators), updated in place; constant memory & recurrent / linear family
ring & capacity-bounded K/V with a pinned sink region & sliding-window family
conv_tail & last \(k-1\) pre-convolution rows (FIFO) & causal short convolutions
token_tail & last \(n\) token ids & Engram n-gram lookup

Capability Registry

One frozen record per layer_pattern enum value declares whether and how a layer caches: \[\textsc{CacheSpec} \;=\; \big(\texttt{supported},\ \texttt{slot\_\allowbreak type},\ \texttt{slot\_\allowbreak types},\ \texttt{extras},\ \texttt{notes}\big).\] The registry is the single source of truth consulted both at runtime (slot resolution) and statically (configuration warnings). A layer receives a slot only when its mixer’s formulation admits a cache and an incremental branch is implemented and parity-tested; otherwise it receives None and executes the legacy path. The registry is therefore also the project’s honest inventory of what caching means for each paper: supported records the source formulation, the implemented set records engineering status, and notes records the reason.

Forward Plumbing and Fallback Semantics

All signature changes are additive and default to the legacy behaviour: \[\begin{aligned} f_{\text{mixer}}&(\mathbf{x}; \ell, \text{pe}, \texttt{cache}=\varnothing, \texttt{cache\_\allowbreak position}=\varnothing),\\ f_{\text{model}}&(\mathbf{x}; \texttt{past\_\allowbreak key\_\allowbreak values}=\varnothing, \texttt{use\_\allowbreak cache}=\bot, \texttt{return\_\allowbreak cache}=\bot). \end{aligned}\] HybridLayer resolves the slot once per call and honours the four historical dispatch shapes: stateless linear (mamba) is called without arguments because it has nothing to cache; the two whole-stream mixers (ode, retnet) receive the slot only when their spec supports it; Engram additionally receives input_ids; every other mixer receives cache and cache_position. Unsupported or disabled layers are called exactly as before, which keeps the uncached path bit-identical.

Correctness Contracts

Cached and uncached execution must agree on the query row they share: the last row of a full forward and the row produced by a decode step. The contracts below establish that agreement.

Post-RoPE Storage and the Absolute Schedule

Keys are stored after the rotary transform, the industry convention: the cache holds the rotated vectors, and no re-rotation is needed when a ring buffer wraps. The prerequisite is that rotation use absolute positions on both sides of the cache boundary. RoPE, HoPE and sinusoidal-rotary accept a position offset \(\pi_0\) and place the incoming tokens at \[\pi_i = \big(\pi_0 + i\big)\cdot \texttt{scaling}, \qquad i = 0,\dots,S_{\text{new}}-1 ,\] so a decode step at cursor \(p\) rotates exactly as the full forward rotated position \(p\). The slot metadata versions the scaling factor; a runtime change of the RoPE schedule invalidates already-rotated keys and is reported as a configuration error at generation start, never mid-decode .

Additive Score Biases

ALiBi and BAM inject position through the score matrix, so they carry no positional tensor in the cache — precisely their appeal for length extrapolation . The full-square builder generalizes to a windowed builder over absolute query and key positions: \[b_{h,i,j} \;=\; -\,\text{slope}_h \cdot \big|q_i - \kappa_j\big| \quad\text{(ALiBi)}, \qquad b_{h,i,j} \;=\; -\Big(\big|\kappa_j - \alpha_h q_i - \mu_h\big| + \varepsilon\Big)^{\beta_h} \quad\text{(BAM)},\] where \(q_i = \pi_0 + i\) for the incoming query positions and \(\kappa_j\) are the cached absolute key positions. With \(\pi_0 = 0\) and \(\kappa_j = j\) this reproduces the legacy matrix exactly; after eviction, \(\kappa_j\) may be non-contiguous, and the distances remain correct by construction.

Length-Dependent Rescaling

Scalable Softmax multiplies pre-softmax logits by \(s\cdot\ln n\) where \(n\) is the context length. In cached decoding the context of the newest query is the accumulated cache, so the rescale uses \[\ln\big(n_{\text{cached}} + S_{\text{new}}\big)\] rather than the size of the incoming chunk. For the final row of a full forward over \(S_{\text{cached}}+S_{\text{new}}\) tokens both expressions coincide, which is exactly the row the parity tests compare.

Causal Masking from Positions

Masks are derived from metadata rather than from array indices: \[M_{ij} \;=\; \big[\,q_i < \kappa_j\,\big] \;=\; \big[\,\pi_0 + i < \kappa_j\,\big],\] which reduces to the classical upper-triangular mask when the cache starts empty and \(\kappa_j = j\). For a single decode query every cached key satisfies \(\kappa_j \le q_i\), so the mask is empty and the step needs no mask at all. Sparse families replace the causal predicate with a position-based pattern (§28.4).

Absolute Positional Encodings

Additive absolute encodings (sinusoidal, learned) are applied once to the embeddings. In cached decoding the embedding lookup for the new token receives the same offset, so token \(p\) is augmented with row \(p\) of the table: \[\mathbf{x}_i \;\leftarrow\; \mathbf{x}_i + \text{PE}\big[\pi_0 + i\big].\]

Interlocks with Mixture-of-Depths, mHC, Hyperloop and AttnRes

Mixture-of-Depths routes a fraction of tokens through each layer. Routing a prompt would produce ragged, token-dependent caches, which v1 deliberately excludes; when the cache is active, prefill is forced dense while decode degenerates to dense automatically (one token is always within capacity). The divergence is one-directional: forcing dense can only add keys, never attend to keys that do not exist. mHC and Hyperloop residual streams are per-token state and flow through a cached forward without cross-step carry; the loop-level hyper-connections fire per iteration and need no slot of their own. Attention-residual variants keep cross-layer buffers that must accumulate across steps, a mode not yet implemented; the combination disables caching for that forward with a warning and falls back to full recompute. PaPE augmentations are content-dependent, so caching post-augmentation keys is not provably exact; such layers fall back per layer .

Incremental Recipes by Family

Quadratic Softmax Family

For a dense attention layer with \(H\) query heads, \(H_{kv}\) key/value heads and head dimension \(d\), the cached branch appends the new keys and values and attends over the whole retained prefix: \[\mathbf{K} \gets \big[\mathbf{K}_{\text{cached}};\ \mathbf{k}_{\text{new}}\big],\quad \mathbf{V} \gets \big[\mathbf{V}_{\text{cached}};\ \mathbf{v}_{\text{new}}\big],\quad \mathbf{S} = \frac{\mathbf{q}\mathbf{K}^\top}{\sqrt d} + \mathbf{B},\quad \mathbf{o} = \operatorname{softmax}(\mathbf{S})\,\mathbf{V},\] with \(\mathbf{B}\) the positional bias of §28.3. Grouped-query attention caches only the \(H_{kv}\) compact heads and expands head groups after the read, which is where its cache advantage originates . The family’s variations are all captured by substituting the normalizer or the bias:

  • Sigmoid attention. The normalizer is replaced by an \(\ell_1\) row normalization, \(\hat{\mathbf{S}}_{ij} = \sigma(\mathbf{S}_{ij}) / \big(\sum_{j'}\sigma(\mathbf{S}_{ij'}) + \varepsilon\big)\). Because sigmoid is not shift-invariant, the denominator must be re-summed over the full cached prefix at every step; no online-softmax maximum trick exists .

  • Gated softmax. The gate \(\sigma(\mathbf{x}\mathbf{W}_g)\) multiplies the attention output and depends only on the current token, so nothing extra is cached .

  • Forgetting attention. The logit bias is \(D_{ij} = c_i - c_j\) with \(c_i = \sum_{l\le i}\log f_l\) the cumulative log-forget sum. The cache stores one scalar per token and head as an extra; decode extends the running sum from the last cached token and evaluates a single row of \(D\) against the cached column .

  • Titans. The implemented layer is the attention window; the memory module is outside the cached path. Standard append/read applies .

  • Memory Attention. Class (i): prefill caches the post-RoPE keys and the constructed values \(V = K + \mathrm{RMSNorm}(E[s])\), so decode looks up only the new token’s memory row and the slot is byte-identical to standard KV .

  • Interleaved head attention. Pseudo-key/value tensors are static learned head mixings computed on the fly; only the real per-token K/V is cached, and the mixing is applied after the read (the mixing is a per-token head-space map, so applying it post-read is exact) .

Latent Family

Latent mixers compress keys and values into a low-rank latent and cache only that latent. Writing \(\mathbf{c}_{KV} = \mathbf{W}_{DKV}\mathbf{x}\), decode re-expands and rotates per step: \[\mathbf{k} = \mathbf{W}_{UK}\mathbf{c}_{KV},\qquad \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{W}_{UV}\mathbf{c}_{KV},\qquad [\mathbf{q},\mathbf{k}] \leftarrow \operatorname{RoPE}\big([\mathbf{q},\mathbf{k}], \pi_0\big),\] with attention as in the dense case . DeepSeek-style MLA caches a decoupled RoPE key and can absorb the up-projections into the query, avoiding per-step expansion; this toolkit’s variant applies RoPE to the decompressed query and key, so absorption is unavailable and expansion is the documented cost of halving the cache. GQLA reuses one weight set with two algebraically equivalent decode paths, and the slot layout follows the configured path . MLRA partitions the latent into disjoint sub-heads, which is a tensor-parallel sharding win rather than a compression win; the total cache is MLA-sized . Tucker attention caches the factorized key and value latents and expands through the core projections . GTA caches one key per head group plus latent values; because rotation at a fixed position is head-independent, group means commute with the rotation and caching the mean is exact . MTLA is the only method that compresses along time: a hyper-network merges adjacent cache vectors at stride boundaries, the schedule is dynamic, and its parity with a chunk-level training schedule is a named risk, so it currently falls back .

Sparse and Window Families

Sparse patterns are evaluated as predicates over absolute positions, never over array indices : \[\text{attend}(q_i,\kappa_j) ;\Longleftrightarrow; \text{pattern}\big(\pi_0+i,\ \kappa_j\big) \;\wedge\; \kappa_j \le \pi_0+i .\]

  • Sliding window with sinks. Every query attends to the first \(s\) positions plus the last \(w-s\); the ring buffer’s retention policy is the attention pattern, so a decode step attends the cached set directly and a multi-token chunk is pattern-masked . Removing the sinks collapses quality, which is why they are pinned both by the pattern and by the ring.

  • Longformer. Symmetric windows plus task-specified global tokens; because a global token may sit anywhere, the slot is unbounded and the pattern is evaluated over positions .

  • BigBird. Window, globals and random links. Random links must be reproducible across incremental steps, so they are drawn from a generator seeded by \((\ell, q_i)\) over \([0, q_i]\): links beyond the query are causal-masked anyway, so the effective mask is unchanged while becoming deterministic .

  • Sparse Transformers. Strided and fixed factorized patterns, where a token’s summary-column role changes as blocks complete; position-based evaluation handles this, and an automatic stride is resolved from the accumulated length so the full and cached paths agree .

  • FASA. Per-head importance is computed from dominant RoPE-frequency chunks and re-ranked per query; it is row-local, so a decode step re-ranks the cached keys exactly . SpargeAttn, NSA, MiniMax and SparDA select blocks from chunk-level statistics and therefore fall back in v1 .

Recurrent and Linear State Family

Recurrent mixers carry a fixed-size state; caching means persisting that state, so memory is constant and no eviction is meaningful. With the paper convention \(\mathbf{S}_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d_v\times d_k}\) and read \(\mathbf{o}_t = \mathbf{S}_t\mathbf{q}_t\):

\[\begin{aligned} \text{RetNet:}\quad & \mathbf{S}_t = \gamma_h\,\mathbf{S}_{t-1} + \mathbf{v}_t\mathbf{k}_t^\top, \qquad \text{per-head multi-scale }\gamma_h, \\ \text{GLA:}\quad & \mathbf{S}_t = \mathbf{G}_t \odot \mathbf{S}_{t-1} + \mathbf{v}_t\mathbf{k}_t^\top, \qquad \mathbf{G}_t = \operatorname{diag}\big(\exp(\operatorname{logsigmoid}(\mathbf{W}_{gk}\mathbf{x}_t)/c)\big), \\ \text{DeltaNet:}\quad & \mathbf{S}_t = \mathbf{S}_{t-1}\big(\mathbf{I} - \beta_t\mathbf{k}_t\mathbf{k}_t^\top\big) + \beta_t\mathbf{v}_t\mathbf{k}_t^\top, \\ \text{Gated DeltaNet:}\quad & \mathbf{S}_t = \alpha_t\,\mathbf{S}_{t-1}\big(\mathbf{I} - \beta_t\mathbf{k}_t\mathbf{k}_t^\top\big) + \beta_t\mathbf{v}_t\mathbf{k}_t^\top, \\ \text{GDN-2:}\quad & \mathbf{S}_t = \big(\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{k}_t(\mathbf{b}_t\odot\mathbf{k}_t)^\top\big)\mathbf{D}_t\mathbf{S}_{t-1} + \mathbf{k}_t(\mathbf{w}_t\odot\mathbf{v}_t)^\top, \\ \text{HGRN2:}\quad & \mathbf{S}_t = \operatorname{diag}(\mathbf{g}_t)\mathbf{S}_{t-1} + \mathbf{v}_t\mathbf{k}_t^\top, \qquad g_{t,j} = b_\ell + (1-b_\ell)\sigma(\cdot), \\ \text{KDA:}\quad & \mathbf{S}_t = \big(\mathbf{I} - \beta_t\mathbf{k}_t\mathbf{k}_t^\top\big)\mathbf{D}_t\mathbf{S}_{t-1} + \beta_t\mathbf{k}_t\mathbf{v}_t^\top, \\ \text{GMA:}\quad & \tilde{\mathbf{V}}_t = \tilde{\mathbf{V}}_{t-1} + \boldsymbol{\gamma}^{K}_t \otimes \mathbf{v}_t,\quad \mathbf{Z}_t = \mathbf{Z}_{t-1} + \boldsymbol{\gamma}^{K}_t, \quad \mathbf{o}_t = \frac{\sum_k \gamma^{Q}_{t,k}\tilde{\mathbf{V}}_{t,k}}{\sum_k \gamma^{Q}_{t,k}Z_{t,k} + \varepsilon}, \end{aligned}\] referring to , , , , , , and .

Two subtleties deserve emphasis. First, RetNet’s parallel retention sum and the recurrence above produce the same row for the same query — algebraically the parallel form factors through the running state — so the cached path may use the recurrent form while the uncached path uses the parallel one, and the parity test compares the shared row. Second, GDN-2 and KDA decay along the key axis (\(\mathbf{D}_t\) multiplies the state from the left), whereas GLA and HGRN2 gate the key axis element-wise; both are diagonal in the key dimension, which is what makes a simple in-place recurrence exact. The ODE-attention block is excluded: its solver re-derives every token’s intermediate state at each integration step, so a converged-state cache cannot reproduce the full path.

Auxiliary State and Documented Fallbacks

Some mixers need a small FIFO beside their activation cache. Falcon’s chunk-parallel variants bound a rehearsal window, so exact continuation requires the last \(B-1\) prefix-aligned pairs; CCA/CCGQA stack two causal convolutions and need the last \(k-1\) pre-convolution latents plus a shifted value; Engram needs the last \(n_{\max}-1\) token ids only. These are the conv_tail and token_tail kinds.

Documented uncached fallbacks. Each entry carries a paper-based rationale in the capability registry and a loader warning when the cache is enabled; none of them can make inference fail.

KV-Cache Quantization

Quantization is a write-time transform: the slot encodes on append and dequantizes on read, so the stored footprint shrinks while the mixer consumes ordinary floating-point tensors. This placement follows the literature and keeps codecs orthogonal to mixers: the same codec serves dense, latent and ring slots, and latent slots may declare a different granularity per stream. Recurrent states are not quantized in v1: the evidence base there is thinnest, and their constant size makes the payoff small.

Symmetric int8 with Asymmetric Axes

Keys exhibit persistent per-channel outliers (a RoPE-frequency structure), while values exhibit per-token outliers. The int8 codec therefore uses different reduction axes: \[\text{keys (channel axis):}\quad s_{h,c} = \frac{\max_{t\in g}|K_{t,h,c}|}{127},\qquad \hat{K} = \operatorname{round}\!\big(K/s\big)\in[-127,127];\] \[\text{values (token axis):}\quad s_{t,h} = \frac{\max_{c}|V_{t,h,c}|}{127},\qquad \hat{V} = \operatorname{round}\!\big(V/s\big)\in[-127,127].\] Each stored block carries its own scales, so a token-by-token decode block gets exact per-token scales and the relative rounding error stays bounded by \(1/127\approx 0.8\%\) independently of block size. Dequantization is \(\hat{K}\odot s\); merging two payloads is dequantize, concatenate along time, and requantize.

Group-Wise int4 with a Protected Window

The int4_kivi codec combines KIVI’s group-wise low-bit quantization with the two-region protection pattern of streaming sinks and SKVQ. Signed levels are \([-7,7]\); \(g\) tokens form a group along time; granularity follows the int8 codec. Two regions are kept in full precision:

  • the most recent \(w_p\) tokens (the protected window), never quantized;

  • the first \(s\) tokens (sinks), never quantized and never evicted.

Append semantics mirror KIVI’s residual window: a decode step pushes rows into the full-precision window, and as soon as the oldest chunk completes a group of \(g\) tokens that group is quantized and moved into the history; prefill quantizes whole groups immediately. Reading concatenates \([\text{quantized history}\mid\text{protected window}]\). With signed 4-bit levels, the worst-case absolute error of a group quantizer is half a step, \[|K-\hat{K}| \;\le\; \frac{s}{2} \;=\; \frac{\max_{g}|K|}{2\cdot 7} \;\approx\; 7.1\%\ \text{of the group maximum},\] which is the bound asserted by the codec tests. Because sinks and the protected window stay exact, the tokens that dominate attention mass are never perturbed .

Interface and Future Codecs

Both codecs implement the same three-method contract: encode_write, decode_read and update. Codecs must never raise on unknown tensors: on any internal error they fall back to identity and record a one-time warning, preserving D5 at the storage layer as well. The v1 registry contains none, int8 and int4_kivi; further methods are interface-ready but deliberately unimplemented, and requesting one is a configuration error at generation start: int2_kivi (2-bit with dual-axis variance normalization), palu_lowrank (rank-\(r\) projection with reconstruction), commvq (RoPE-commutative codebooks, attention in codebook space), qjl_sketch (1-bit Johnson–Lindenstrauss signs with an unbiased inner-product estimator) and block_gtq (per-RoPE-frequency bit allocation). Slot metadata already records the positional-encoding type and the scaling version, which is what a codebook or pre-RoPE codec needs to declare its compatibility. Sensitivity-aware per-layer bit allocation (k_bits \(\ne\) v_bits) is exposed by configuration, since attention mass is pyramidal in depth.

Compression and Eviction

Eviction is a read-time transform; keeping it orthogonal to quantization is what allows a quantized cache to be evicted and an evicted cache to be quantized. The v1 policy is StreamingLLM’s window-with-sinks: pin the first \(s\) positions, retain the last \(w\) positions, drop everything in between. The retained budget is \[\mathcal{B} \;=\; s + w ,\] optionally overridden per layer by a budget vector \(\mathcal{B}_\ell\) (attention mass is pyramidal in depth, so deeper layers tolerate smaller budgets). Policies act only on position-indexed slots; recurrent states are constant-size and MTLA manages its own merging schedule, so external policies are excluded there by construction. Future enum-ready policies are H2O (accumulate per-token attention mass and evict the lightest), SnapKV (one-shot post-prefill compression from a look-ahead window), PyramidKV (static depth-dependent budgets) and SparseK (learned scorer with permanent within-generation eviction, which is why it is modeled as a policy rather than a slot).

Configuration and Deployment Interface

The runtime block is validated by a dedicated schema module and flattened into a runtime dataclass that is deliberately not part of the architectural configuration, mirroring the training.* separation.

Resolution order is CLI flags \(>\) YAML inference: \(>\) schema defaults. Every CLI flag defaults to “unset”, so a YAML preset is patched leaf-by-leaf rather than replaced:

infer –task causal_lm –config <preset> –prompt "…" –kv-cache –kv-quant int4_kivi –kv-compress window_sinks –kv-window 512

The deployer serializes the resolved block into the artifact’s config.json under "inference", and the inference engine reads it back, so cached generation is reproducible without the original YAML. The HuggingFace export’s causal-LM wrapper accepts past_key_values, use_cache and cache_position and forwards them to the decoder instead of discarding extras, and implements prepare_inputs_for_generation so that a standard transformers loop feeds only the last token once a cache exists.

Validation

The central test is a parity protocol: for a mixer and a positional encoding, compare a full forward over \(S\) tokens against prefill over \(S-k\) tokens followed by \(k\) decode steps, requiring agreement on the shared row. Greedy generation is compared token-for-token first; if a numerical discrepancy appears, last-position logits are compared with \(\mathrm{rtol}=10^{-4}\), \(\mathrm{atol}=10^{-5}\) in fp32 with quantizer none and BitNet disabled.

Validation matrix. The registry is also cross-checked against the schema’s layer-pattern enum so a new mixer cannot be added without a cache decision.
